root_cause.text: `mt7996_mac_write_txwi_80211()` in the mt76/mt7996 Wi-Fi driver accessed `struct ieee80211_mgmt` action/addba request fields without first verifying that the `skb` was long enough, allowing an out-of-bounds read on short management frames.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1` to the `if (ieee80211_is_action(fc) && ... mgmt->u.action.category == ... && mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code == ...)` check in `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/mac.c`, and the commit message explicitly says it fixes a “possible oob access” by checking the frame length before accessing the mgmt fields.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a packet-length guard before parsing ADDBA action frame fields to avoid invalid memory access on short frames.
intent_record.what: A new length check, `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1`, was added to the `if` condition in `mt7996_mac_write_txwi_80211()` before accessing `mgmt->u.action.category` and `mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now only interprets an action frame as a Block Ack ADDBA request when the skb is long enough to contain the required action frame fields, preventing reads past the end of a short or malformed packet.

grouping_result.intent: Add a packet-length guard before parsing ADDBA action frame fields to avoid invalid memory access on short frames.
